newsitem.title: FINLAND: Cultor sells acid business to Cargill.
newsitem.headline: Cultor sells acid business to Cargill.

text.p: Finnish sweetener, animal feed and bakery group Cultor Oy said in a statement on Tuesday it would sell its itaconic acid business to privately held U.S. Cargill Inc in a deal worth more than 200 million markka.
"Cultor Food Science ... has entered into an agreement to sell its itaconic acid business to Cargill Inc," Cultor said.

"The net sales of the itaconic acid in 1996 are about 150 million markka. The total value of the transaction is in excess of 200 million markka and the book value of goodwill in the Cultor group from the Food Science Group acquisition will be reduced by about 150 million markka," it said.

"The divestiture of the itaconic acid business is an important strategic step that continues to sharpen Cultor Food Science's focus on specific food industry needs, namely flavourings, food protection and nutritional enhancement," Cultor said.

Itaconic acid is used in the production of synthetic latexes to improve emulsion stability and adhesion, it said, adding the paper-coating and carpet-backing industries were primary users of itaconic acid.
Cultor acquired the Food Science Group from U.S. Pfizer in January. It has said goodwill including intangible assets totalled about $150 million which would be depreciated within 15 years.
